hook.line: Tomás is staring at his first Spanish essay. Everything is hard in some way, and English says "hard to do" without a care. Spanish has two shapes for it, and this is the first one.
hook.es: Este ensayo es difícil de escribir.
hook.en: This essay is hard to write.

examples.en: This word is hard to pronounce.

rule:
Start with the thing, then *ser*, then the adjective, then *de* and an infinitive.

*La palabra es difícil de pronunciar.*

English says "to pronounce" with nothing in between. Spanish needs the little *de*. The thing you talk about is the subject, so the adjective matches it: *fácil* and *fáciles*, *difícil* and *difíciles*.

The same frame works with *imposible*, *agradable*, *raro*, *posible*: *Un libro agradable de leer*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this *de* plus infinitive after an adjective, a complement of the adjective.

options: It's easy to make coffee.
The coffee is easy to make.

readAndPick.es: Esta palabra es difícil de pronunciar.
options: This word is hard to pronounce.
This word is hard, so I pronounce it.
Pronouncing is hard for this word.
Hernando convinces people with difficulty.
Hernando is hard to convince.
Hernando is hard, so he convinces.

readAndPick.es: Es una historia difícil de creer.
options: It's a hard story to believe.
It's hard to tell a story.
It's a hard story to tell.

Writing essays is hard.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (This word is hard to pronounce): *Esta palabra es difícil ___ pronunciar.* (*de* or *a*)
yourTurn.answer: Esta palabra es difícil de pronunciar.
yourTurn.why: After the adjective, Spanish links the infinitive with *de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The problem is easy to fix.
yourTurn.answer: El problema es fácil de resolver.
yourTurn.why: The problem is the subject, so *fácil* matches it and *de* leads into *resolver*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: This essay is hard to write.
yourTurn.answer: Este ensayo es difícil de escribir.
yourTurn.why: The essay is the subject: *ensayo* is masculine, so *este* and *difícil*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The questions are easy to answer.
yourTurn.answer: Las preguntas son fáciles de responder.
yourTurn.why: The questions are plural, so *son* and *fáciles*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural (These essays are hard to write): *Este ensayo es difícil de escribir.*
yourTurn.answer: Estos ensayos son difíciles de escribir.
yourTurn.why: Everything before *de* turns plural, but the infinitive never changes.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative (The problem isn't easy to fix): *El problema es fácil de resolver.*
yourTurn.answer: El problema no es fácil de resolver.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando is hard to convince.
yourTurn.why: Hernando is the subject, and *de convencer* says what is hard about him.

pitfalls.right: Esta palabra es difícil de pronunciar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When the thing is the subject, Spanish needs *de* before the infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Las preguntas son difícil de responder.
pitfalls.right: Las preguntas son difíciles de responder.
pitfalls.why: The adjective describes the questions, so it is plural too.

pitfalls.wrong: Este ensayo es difícil de escribirlo.
pitfalls.right: Este ensayo es difícil de escribir.
pitfalls.why: The essay is already the subject, so no *lo* is needed after the infinitive.

personal: Tell us one thing in your life that is hard or easy, using *de* and an infinitive, for example *Mi jefe es difícil de convencer*.
